script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

A FAMILY of five: PATRICK (40s, ambitious father), MARY (30s, devoted mother), TOM (16, responsible eldest), ANNA (13, rebellious middle), and SAM (8, innocent youngest), sit together on their plush, grey couch. The only light in the room comes from the Christmas tree in the corner.

MARY
(smiling)
Boys and Anna, what do you want for Christmas this year?

TOM
(thoughtful)
I want a new car for my driving lessons.

ANNA
(rolling her eyes)
I just want you all to leave me alone.

SAM
(excited)
I want a toy train set!

Patrick looks at his children, trying to decide which of their wishes he can fulfill.

PATRICK
We'll see, kids. But remember, with ambition comes responsibility.

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

Mary stands at the kitchen counter, cutting vegetables for dinner. Patrick enters, holding a stack of papers.

PATRICK
Mary, I've got some news. The company is expanding, and I've been asked to take on a larger role. I'll be traveling more often.

MARY
(concerned)
That's wonderful, dear. But what about us? The kids?

PATRICK
(comforting)
Don't worry, I'll make it work. I promise.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

The family gathers around the Christmas tree, their eyes filled with excitement as they exchange presents. Tom receives driving lessons, Anna gets a journal, and Sam gets his toy train set.

ANNA
(disappointed)
That's it? A journal?

PATRICK
(looking at Anna)
What do you want me to do, Anna? Buy you a sports car? This is about learning and growing.

ANNA
(defeated)
I guess I'll try harder.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL - DAY

Tom drives his new car to school, dropping Anna off on the way. She walks in the front door, looking discontent.

Anna approaches the guidance counselor's desk.

ANNA
I want to drop out of school.

GUIDANCE COUNSELOR
(concerned)
Anna, why do you want to do that?

ANNA
(angrily)
Because my family doesn't care about me!

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Patrick sits on the couch, feeling defeated. Mary enters, holding a stack of papers.

MARY
Patrick, I've got some news. The company is laying off employees, and unfortunately, I've been let go.

PATRICK
(shocked)
What are we going to do?

MARY
(determined)
We'll figure it out. We'll all chip in and help out where we can.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL - DAY

Tom and Anna sit in the school cafeteria, surrounded by their friends. Tom looks at Anna, who looks unhappy.

TOM
Anna, what's going on? You've been acting out lately.

ANNA
(frustrated)
I'm just tired of everything. Feeling like I don't matter.

TOM
(thoughtful)
Maybe it's time for a change. What do you want to do?

ANNA
(excited)
I want to start my own business. A bakery!

Tom smiles, proud of his sister's ambition.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

The family gathers around the Christmas tree, the room filled with candles and warmth. Patrick and Mary exchange a look, knowing that they'll get through this together.

PATRICK
(smiling)
Boys and Anna, remember what I said earlier? With ambition comes responsibility. But it also brings love, growth, and the opportunity to make a difference in the world.

ANNA
(smiling back)
I get it now, Dad.

The family shares a moment of understanding, their love for each other shining brighter than the tree.

FADE OUT.
